description: The line plot illustrates the accuracy (ACC) of five different methods—Base, MEND, FT, MEMIT, and IKE—across varying co-occurrence numbers, with the x-axis representing the co-occurrence number on a logarithmic scale ranging from 1 to 1000, and the y-axis showing accuracy in percentage from 60% to 80%. The Base method, represented by a black line with circular markers, starts at approximately 61% accuracy and shows a steady increase, reaching about 66.5% at a co-occurrence number of 1000. The MEND method, shown with a brown line and diamond markers, begins at around 65.5% and gradually increases to approximately 74% at the highest co-occurrence number. The FT method, depicted with a blue line and triangle markers, starts at about 62.5% and rises to roughly 68.5% at the end of the range. The MEMIT method, represented by a purple line with pentagon markers, begins at approximately 66.5% and increases to about 72.5% at the highest co-occurrence number. The IKE method, shown with a red line and triangle markers, starts at around 64.5% and increases to approximately 70% at the highest co-occurrence number. The green line with square markers, representing the highest accuracy, starts at about 72.5% and remains relatively stable, slightly increasing to around 77.5% at the highest co-occurrence number.
